_doc: Q6504: the framing members bim.clash tests the MEP against, and the hole rules each hit is judged by (an allowed bored hole or a real conflict). Flags for coordination only, never a structural approval: the member maker's literature (an I-joist or rim board hole chart, a truss drawing, a stud maker's punchout and hole tables) or the engineer's details override, as project rules do. The I-joist web and truss chord rules are the conduit router's (conduitroute.json `framing`), one source for both.
members_source: the framing trade's pieces a raceway, pipe or duct crosses (studs, joists and I-joists, trusses, rim boards, headers and beams); plates, tracks, blocking, backing and furring are the wall's and floor's own edges and are not tested
no_holes_source: company default: headers, beams and columns are never field bored or notched without the structural engineer's detail (IRC R502.8.2 / IBC 2308.4.2.4: engineered and built-up members only as their design allows)
runs_source: the MEP pieces that pass through a member (a run and its fittings); equipment, terminals and boxes stand in the bay beside it
parallel_source: geometry: a run within 30 degrees of a member's length runs along inside it, not across it
words_source: the member's type and item as the trade layout wrote them (`I-joist`, `floor truss`, `wood 2x6`, `steel 20 ga`); a joist that names no sawn lumber is the layout's engineered I-joist (tradeatoms.json joist_depth_source)

sawn_joist.source: IRC R502.8.1 / IBC 2308.4.2.4: holes bored in sawn lumber joists no larger than 1/3 of the depth and no closer than 2 in to the top or bottom; the hole is the outside size plus 3/8 in (the conduit router's hole allowance)

rim.source: company default from the rim board makers' published hole rules (a round hole up to 1/3 of the board's depth, kept off its edges); the rim board submittal's own chart overrides (project rule)

wood_stud.source: IRC R602.6: holes bored in a wood stud no larger than 40% of its width in a bearing wall (60% in a non-bearing partition), the hole's edge no closer than 5/8 in to the stud's face; a wall whose type says neither is taken as bearing (the stricter limit) and the reason says so

steel_stud.source: company default: a cold-formed steel stud is passed through its factory punchouts (1 1/2 in wide, in the middle of the web, ASTM C645 / SSMA standard punchouts); anything larger needs a field-cut hole by the stud maker's limits or a reinforced opening
